newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos sets tasks before 1998 bow out.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos sets tasks before 1998 bow out.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Thursday vowed to solve Manila's chaotic traffic situation and reform the country's individual and corporate tax laws before bowing out of office in 18 months' time.

He said his remaining agenda also called for liberalising retail trade and the finance sector, offering better incentives for investors to set up regional headquarters in the country, a stronger intellectual property rights law to curb piracies and a law that would allow foreigners to own land.
"These reforms will tear down the remaining structural and institutional barriers to growth and they will complete the policy architecture for sustained development," Ramos told businessmen.
Before stepping down in June 1998, Ramos said, he hoped to have in place a modern mass transport system for Manila and other urban centres.
"Your traffic woes will also be mine 18 months from now as a car owner-driver," he said.
Ramos has previously liberalised the telecommunications, banking and energy sectors, helping spur the country's dramatic economic growth in the past three years, economists said.
"We can look forward to better years in 1997 and 1988," Ramos said. "The regime of boom and bust is over for the Philippines."
